To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have measured open-loop roll, yaw and pitch torques for a flapping-wing micro air vehicle (MAV).
we have measured roll, pitch and pitch/yaw torques of an insect-sized robotic flying vehicle and demonstrated open-loop flight maneuvers.
we have developed a new actuation method that can be used to control the roll and pitch motion of flapping wings, which is a key component of the flight control system for a robotic insect.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of small-scale robotic systems that can be used to study insect flight and to explore new applications in microrobotics.
the development of a small-scale, insect-sized robotic platform that can be used for studying insect flight control and aerodynamics.
the design of flapping wing mechanisms that can generate sufficient roll and pitch torques to enable flight control.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have successfully developed a robotic bee that can hover and perform open-loop maneuvers.
this paper is the first to report on open-loop roll, yaw and pitch torques for an insect-sized flapping-wing vehicle, and that these torques are sufficient to generate open-loop flight maneuvers.
this work is the first to present measurements of open-loop pitch, roll and yaw torques and flight experiments for an autonomous, insect-sized robotic bee.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the torque measurements show that our actuators are capable of generating sufficient torque for flight and that the open loop flight tests demonstrate the ability of the actuators to generate sufficient roll and pitch moments for flight maneuvers.
we are the first to measure and control the roll, pitch and roll-pitch coupling for a robotic bee.
we have demonstrated that a flapping wing mechanism can be used for control and stabilization.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the open-loop torques generated with this design are sufficient for flight, and the flight experiments show that the control system can be designed in such a way that it is robust to the uncertainties in the open-loop torque model.

the flapping-wing actuation scheme we use can generate significant torques for roll, pitch, and yaw, and that it is possible to achieve liftoff and open-loop control of the roll and pitch axes for the lighter prototype.
the torque generation capability of a robotic bee is comparable to that of a real insect.
